title: Connexions de Gauss-Manin et équations de Picard-Fuchs. Opération de Cartier : copies de tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), tiré à part (1981), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: f: X -> S is smooth and proper, S has characteristic p, and Frobenius twists are written (p/S). Notation from the surrounding pages: P^{ci} = Pic^{ci}_{X/S} classifies invertible sheaves with integrable connection (Pic^natural). P^{cin} classifies those whose connection has nilpotent p-curvature. Pic^{cip} classifies those with p-curvature zero; by Cartier descent, Pic^{cip} = F^*Pic_{X^{(p/S)}}. On the previous page, p-curvature is a homomorphism Pic^{ci} -> f_*(Omega^1) twisted by Frobenius, to a vector group. Its kernel is Pic^{cip} (4.1). Pic^{cin} is the preimage of the 'formal group' (nilpotent sections) of that vector group (4.2-4.3). The cokernel and kernel pieces are analysed via closed 1-forms modulo dlog, and the Cartier sheaf appears in (4.5) (Katz's formula: p-curvature = w^{(p)} - C(w)).

This page does three things.
(i) Cart_{X/S} in (4.5) is the Cartier sheaf already met in (3.2).
(ii) Take the subfunctor of P^{cin} lying over Pic^0_{X/S}. Assume Pic^0 is 'V-divisible', e.g. an abelian scheme, so Verschiebung (Pic^0)^{(p/S)} -> Pic^0 is an epimorphism. Since Frobenius pull-back of a line bundle carries a canonical connection with zero p-curvature, every point of Pic^0 lifts to P^{cin}. This gives (4.6): 0 -> U -> [P^{cin}]^0 -> Pic^0 -> 0, with U the 'vectorial/formal' part studied via (4.4)-(4.5).
(iii) NB. For rank one, nilpotent p-curvature means the p-curvature section is nilpotent. So P^{cin} is the formal completion of P^{ci} along the closed subgroup Pic^{cip} = F^*Pic_{X^{(p/S)}}, which is the zero fibre of the p-curvature map (the rank-1 'p-Hitchin map'). Equivalently, P^{cin} is the crystalline Picard functor: invertible crystals = line bundles with connection of nilpotent p-curvature.

Favourable case: the identity component of P^{ci} is the universal vector extension 0 -> V -> E -> B -> 0 of an abelian scheme B. The Frobenius-pull-back map B^{(p/S)} -> E is a closed immersion (Cartier descent) lifting Verschiebung. So P^{cin,0} is the formal completion of E along the abelian subscheme B^{(p/S)}. Grothendieck stresses that this is much finer information than the formal group Ê (completion of E at the unit section).

Purpose: describe the crystalline Picard scheme / Dieudonné-type invariants of Pic^0 in terms of the universal vector extension, as part of the Gauss-Manin / Cartier operator programme.
errors: The NB as written is circular ('P^{cin} is the completion of P^{cin} ≃ Pic^{(p/S)} in P^{ci}'). The intended statement must be: P^{cin} is the completion of P^{ci} along the subgroup Pic^{cip} ≃ F^*Pic_{X^{(p/S)}}. The superscript (p/S) refers to the Frobenius-twisted Picard group.
That B^{(p/S)} -> E is a closed immersion (not just a homomorphism lifting V) relies on Cartier descent being fully faithful. This holds, but is not stated.

Identifying 'nilpotent p-curvature' with the formal completion along the zero fibre is fine as an ind-scheme / formal-scheme statement. Over non-reduced bases, 'nilpotent' has to be understood locally (formal completion of the vector group at 0); this is left implicit.

ideas.what: Rank-one p-curvature as a homomorphism Pic^natural -> vector group H^0(X', Omega^1). Its kernel is F^*Pic_{X'}, and the line bundles with nilpotent p-curvature form the formal completion along that kernel.
ideas.modern_name: Rank-one p-Hitchin map / p-curvature map; crystalline Picard as formal neighbourhood of the zero fibre
ideas.usually_credited_to: Katz (p-curvature, 1970); for moduli: Laszlo–Pauly, Bezrukavnikov–Braverman (2007), Groechenig (2016)

ideas.what: V-divisibility of Pic^0 makes the Frobenius-pull-back lift surjective onto Pic^0, giving the extension (4.6).
ideas.modern_name: Verschiebung lift of Pic^0 into the universal vector extension
ideas.usually_credited_to: Mazur–Messing 1974 (universal extensions and crystalline Dieudonné theory)
ideas.where_published: Possibly related material in Grothendieck, 'Groupes de Barsotti-Tate et cristaux de Dieudonné' (Montréal 1970)

ideas.what: In the abelian-scheme case, Pic of crystals (identity component) = formal completion of the universal vector extension E along the abelian subscheme B^{(p)} embedded via Frobenius pull-back. This is finer than the formal group Ê.
ideas.modern_name: Formal tube of E along B^{(p)}; crystalline universal extension

ideas.what: Cartier sheaf as kernel piece in the dévissage of the 'vector' part.
ideas.modern_name: Cartier operator / Katz's formula psi = w^p - C(w)

missed.claim: Explicit description of the crystalline Picard functor (rank-one crystals) as the formal completion of the de Rham Picard Pic^natural along the zero fibre of the p-curvature homomorphism. In the abelian case it is the completion of the universal vector extension E along the abelian subscheme B^{(p)} = Frobenius pull-backs. This anticipates the 'rank-one p-Hitchin map' viewpoint of later non-abelian Hodge theory in char p, and stresses that it carries strictly more information than the formal group of E.
missed.quote: on trouve que P^{cin°}_{X/S} est le complété formel le long B^{p/S}. Sa connaissance est donc nettement plus précise que celle du complété formel Ê de E le long de sa section unité
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Gives a geometric 'formal tube' model of rank-one crystals inside the universal vector extension. This could be compared with Ogus–Vologodsky, Groechenig's rank-one analysis, and crystalline Dieudonné theory. Most ingredients are known, but this specific formulation and its 1972 date may predate the published sources.

deep.surprise_reason: Coherent, early (c. 1972) and conceptually sharp. P^{cin} is identified as the formal neighbourhood of Frobenius pull-backs inside Pic^natural, and the extension structure over Pic^0 is set out. The ingredients (Katz p-curvature, Cartier descent, Mazur–Messing universal extension) are standard or were published soon after, so the novelty is mostly in the formulation and dating.
transcription_corrections: The superscript is 'cin' (connexion intégrable nilpotente), not 'cris': read P^{cin}_{X/S} throughout, and P^{cin°} for the identity component.
'Ric' in the neighbouring transcriptions is 'Pic' (underlined Pic).
In the NB, 'P^♮' is likely written 'P^{ci}' on the page: 'P^{cin}_{X/S} ≃ Pic^{♮(p/S)}_{X/S} ⊂ P^{ci} dans P^{ci}'.
'Regardons les deux foncteurs de P^{cin}' is more likely 'Regardons le sous-foncteur de P^{cin} image inverse de Pic°'.
'(gr. sur schéma abélien)' is plausibly '(p. ex. un schéma abélien)'.
'B^{p/S}' should be read as the Frobenius twist B^{(p/S)}.
